title: My next vibecoded game. Took me three months. I give up :)
author: Master-Client6682
selftext:
I’ve been vibecoding a word game called **WordStrata** for about 3 months and I think it’s finally at the stage where it’s worth other people playing.

I built it using a mixture of ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini. A lot of the process was me bouncing between them asking for bug checks, implementing ideas, and debugging help. The bigger part though was just **playing the game constantly** and tweaking it toward what *I* found fun.

I didn’t set out to make a commercial product. I basically made the word roguelike I personally wanted to exist.

It ended up being way more complicated than my first vibecoded game, WordQuest:  
[https://splarg.itch.io/word-quest](https://splarg.itch.io/word-quest)

WordStrata is a simple roguelike word game with three modes:

• **Normal Mode** – Reach level 50, score as much as possible, optimise your word choices  
• **Survival Mode** – Fight against an O₂ drain by making words to stay alive  
• **Challenge Mode** – Survival but players share the same seed/keys so you can compete directly

I learned a ridiculous amount making this. Turns out even “simple” word games get complex fast once you add progression systems, balance, stats tracking, scaling difficulty, etc.

I’m not trying to make money from it. I’m not really looking for anything in particular. I just genuinely enjoy making and playing these kinds of games.

Honestly it reminds me of old public domain / shareware Amiga games. I used to save up pocket money, buy random weird little games, rush home, and if they were terrible… tough. That was part of the charm. I also loved WordJong on the DS, which definitely sits in the same spirit as this.

This is basically my small contribution to that tradition.

If anyone wants to try it, give feedback, break it, suggest ideas, or just chase scores, you’re very welcome to:

👉 [https://splarg.itch.io/wordstrata](https://splarg.itch.io/wordstrata)

I’m still actively improving it based on play experience, so player feedback genuinely helps shape what it becomes.

Thanks for reading 🙂

comments.author: Lucky-Space6065
comments.body: Looks good.  I'm not a word puzzle guy, but ran great.  Ui was nice, visuals pleasant.  I'd call that a win

replies.author: Master-Client6682
replies.body: Thanks dude. Yeah it's all about playtesting and adapting. People hate on vibecoding and ai, but they helped me make something. I worked on it till i was happy. Do i need to understand each and every line? No.

comments.author: jgesq
comments.body: Really enjoyed it. A great game. Wasn’t sure how to quit or save or give up when I couldn’t make anymore words.

replies.author: Master-Client6682
replies.body: thanks for the feedback. I put stuff in the pause menu but it's a bit hidden. touch the logo . Aj kept talking about tutorials but it all seemed overkill. You very rarely die in normal mode. And you can't save in survival. Gives me things to think about. 👍

replies.author: jgesq
replies.body: Well, keep it up. And let me know when you drop it off for sale.

replies.author: Master-Client6682
replies.body: Thanks dude. Am not intending to monetise it. I made it for myself. A game i can play on the bus. I just thought others might enjoy it...

comments.author: Osirian_Legacy
comments.body: I’d keep working on it, get a dedicated artist and then make this into a mobile game. If you wanna make money from it offer skins to customize how it looks. Otherwise just the game itself is pretty cool.

replies.author: Master-Client6682
replies.body: I just made it for me. I missed wordjong and decided to try vibecoding a clone of sorts. it ended up into something different. I don't care about making money. it's a hobby really. bit of fun. thanks for the comments 👍

replies.author: harmonicrain
replies.body: You're like me, I plan on making a call of duty zombies clone and then just opensourcing it on GitHub as GPLv3 lol

replies.author: Master-Client6682
replies.body: Nice dude. At the moment i'm a little bit addicted to making games i want to play...

replies.author: harmonicrain
replies.body: Honestly some people think it's odd to want to make games and not profit from it. Some of us do it for the passion!!

replies.author: Master-Client6682
replies.body: Yeah exactly. I'm just doing it for fun. Why would I want less people to play the games I'm making by locking them behind a paywall...

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body: If you don't actually know how to code and get AI to essentially make you a game it's not really a good idea to start trying to make money from. When/if something goes wrong and you can't get AI to fix it you're going to have a lot of problems and angry customers to deal with unless you want to start paying an actual dev to fix it for you.

comments.author: lubujackson
comments.body: This is fun! I advise putting the "How to Play" at the top as I was getting frustrated how far I had to scroll to see that lol. Also, not sure what your dictionary is, but "June" isn't a word? COME ON

replies.author: Master-Client6682
replies.body: Ha. It's a scrabble dictionary from github. I know right. Zen. Frustrating. :) But afaik June is not in the Scrabble dictionary. So meh...

replies.author: Master-Client6682
replies.body: if you press the green on the main screen it shows some instructions. Also press the logo during play gives you the pause menu...

comments.author: Trashy_io
comments.body:
I've seen your other post before on here, I think its a great project! And this is definitely a great hobby to get into to learn a bunch! 

My favorite part of this hobby (solo) is how one day you are a programmer, next a music composer, and then an artist. Some times all three in a day and much more other hats to wear! 

Have you put any thought into your next project?

replies.author: Master-Client6682
replies.body: dude. this evening I made a whole game. Claude almost one shot it. and yeah I've got lots of ideas. I guess it helps that's I've been playing video games for over 30 years. I am mainly recreating things I want to play.

replies.author: Master-Client6682
replies.body: the dictionary is from github dude. It seems the word is valid in uk scrabble but not us?

replies.author: Master-Client6682
replies.body: Ha. Yeah. I hate that grrr. If you're playing normal there's some really nice stuff that happens when you get to level 50... My wife loves survival. aint nobody got time for that...

comments.body: So you're... not giving up? What's with the title ?
